subtitle: Per-symbol coverage of the C++ <bit> header. SHIPPED 2026-08-25. All 14 catalogued symbols across 16 granular headers plus the umbrella. Back-ported to C++11 and constexpr from C++11 -- ahead of std, which is constexpr from C++20. The constraint is the subtle part: the counting, rotating and power-of-two functions take only the UNSIGNED INTEGER TYPES, a set that excludes bool and every character type, so it is spelled out explicitly rather than derived from is_unsigned. Verified against libstdc++ <bit> at C++20 and self-verified at C++11/14/17.
legend_blurb: <bit> provides bit-level inspection and manipulation of unsigned integers, plus bit_cast for defined object-representation reinterpretation.

symbols.name: endian
symbols.notes: Three enumerators, not two: native equals neither little nor big on a mixed-endian platform, which is the only portable way to detect that case. Uses __BYTE_ORDER__ where available; MSVC targets are all little-endian; otherwise native gets a distinct value rather than guessing. D_RE_STD_HAS_ENDIAN_DETECTION reports which path was taken.
symbols.failure_reason: Ships at C++11, below the workbook C++98 floor. Floor question, not a coverage gap -- the module is currently gated on C++11 and has no C++98 path yet. symbols.name: bit_cast
symbols.notes: Constexpr ONLY where __builtin_bit_cast exists -- the memcpy fallback cannot be made constexpr from library code, so this is the one re_std symbol whose constexpr-ness varies by platform. D_RE_STD_HAS_BUILTIN_BIT_CAST reports it. STOPGAP: the trivially-copyable constraint calls __is_trivially_copyable directly because re_std::is_trivially_copyable is catalogued but not implemented; switch to the trait and delete the local detection when it ships.

symbols.name: byteswap
symbols.notes: Wider constraint than the rest of the module: any integral type, signed and character types included, not just the unsigned integer types. Works on the corresponding unsigned type and casts back, since shifting a negative value is implementation-defined before C++20. A byte is CHAR_BIT bits from numeric_limits, not assumed to be 8.

symbols.notes: Computed as N - bit_width rather than via __builtin_clz, which is UNDEFINED at zero -- the case callers most often pass. N is numeric_limits<T>::digits, so countl_zero(uint8_t(1)) is 7, not 31.

symbols.name: bit_ceil
symbols.notes: CAN overflow, and the standard says so: undefined when the result is not representable, and then not a constant expression, so a compile-time use is diagnosed and a run-time use is not. No clamp is added -- a wrong answer would be worse than the specified UB.

symbols.name: rotl
symbols.notes: The count is reduced modulo N first: a raw shift by N or more is UB, so this is correctness, not economy. Every sub-expression is cast back to _T or rotl(uint8_t(0x80), 1) yields 0x101 instead of 0x01. Negative counts rotate the other way, per the standard. Split into a *_reduced helper so it stays constexpr at C++11, where a constexpr function may hold only one return.
